segments: The eighteenth cycle.
The Arab kings.
The sword-bearer {OCR?}.
One of the Turkish horsemen related:
"I passed by a door in Muhawwal, a village beside Baghdad,
and behold, a young girl was at the door, weeping and saying:
'Who will rescue me from death and take me? For lo, it has entered our house
and killed my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters.'
And when I entered,
I counted nine dead in that house.
And I was afraid,
and I left and fled.
And when my compassion was stirred for that girl,
and I turned back to take her,
I found her fallen upon her mother's chest, dead (and struck down?)."
And on the twenty-seventh of Elul of this year, which is the year 1396,
1396 of the Greeks,
(1085 of our Lord?),
a black wind blew in Baghdad,
and the air grew dark.
And thick sand was lifted up between earth and heaven,
and it moved like a great mountain through the ether.
And many of the human beings and cattle died, and even wild beasts in the wilderness (desert).
And scoundrels entered the baths
and snatched their clothes,
and they also plundered the markets.
And it sank many ships.
And in the year 479,
479 of the Arabs [AH]:
A battle took place between the Emir Artuq Beg and Suleiman ibn Qutalmish, the master of Antioch.
And he, Suleiman the Sultan, was killed in that battle.
It is said
that when he saw his side was defeated,
he killed himself with a knife.
And thus he was found lying,
with the knife fixed in his belly.
Now the Sultan, when he heard that Suleiman was killed,
set out from Khorasan for Syria.
And the Emir Artuq went to Jerusalem,
and placed his family and his belongings in the Tower of David the King,
and fortified himself there.
Now the Sultan, when he reached Edessa—
which was held by Philaretos—
its inhabitants readily surrendered it.
And Philaretos himself, because he had perceived the hatred of the Edessenes toward him,
had gone to Khorasan to the Sultan.
And since the Sultan had come by another route,
he did not meet him in Persia.
Instead, he turned back, came, and overtook him in Mesopotamia,
after he had taken Edessa.
And he promised to pay tribute,
and to proclaim the Caliph and the Sultan.
And he converted to Islam at the hands of the Sultan,
and was circumcised and fell ill,
and he traveled with the Sultan's camp on litters.
